g1.label: 1. The flat is ___ small for four people.
g1.why: Too before an adjective means more than is good: too small.

g2.label: 2. The room is not big ___ for a desk and a bed.
g2.why: Enough comes after an adjective: big enough.

g3.label: 3. I don’t have ___ time to finish the course this term.
g3.why: Enough comes before a noun: enough time.

g4.label: 4. It is ___ cold to study in the library without a jacket.
g4.why: Too goes before an adjective, and too much needs a noun.

g5.label: 5. There are ___ many people on the bus, so we can’t sit down.
g5.why: Too many goes with countable nouns, so too + many fits here.

g6.label: 6. This app is ___ to use, so even beginners can try it.
g6.why: Enough follows the adjective: easy enough.

g7.label: 7. She is ___ to live alone yet.
g7.why: Not + adjective + enough: not old enough.

g8.label: 8. The rent is too high ___ me to pay.
g8.why: Too high for me to pay: for + person, then to-infinitive.

g9.label: 9. There is ___ noise at night, so I can’t sleep.
g9.why: Noise is uncountable, so use too much.

g10.label: 10. Are there ___ chairs for everyone in the room?
g10.why: Enough before a noun in a question: enough chairs.

g11.label: 11. Out of all the courses I have taken, this is the ___ (interesting).
g11.why: Longer adjectives form the superlative with the most.

g12.label: 12. By the time we arrived, the agent ___ (leave).
g12.why: By the time shows the agent left first: past perfect.
